generated.runtime: tsc emit of every upstream root-level .ts module (index.ts is the extension entry whose createMcpAdapter export the OMA adapter drives — no exclusions), compiled under ESNext/bundler resolution from a staged copy whose relative .ts specifiers were mechanically rewritten to .js, plus verbatim copies of the non-.ts payload the emitted modules reach by URL (mcp-script-worker.mjs, mcp-keyring-helper.cjs, app-bridge.bundle.js, package.json, skills/), then OMA divergence splices applied

utils.js.reason: The OMA boundary seam itself. omaInstallMcpPolicy is called by src/extension/mcp-tools.ts before upstream's factory runs; without an installed policy every helper degrades to upstream's own behavior (globalThis.fetch, process.env, tmpdir, the keyring store selector), so the seam is inert payload under a bare upstream load. Under the policy: omaPermits is deny-by-default (a permit absent from the table is refused); omaRequirePermit refuses `!command` credential sinks in resolveCommandSecret before any shell runs, covering env, header, bearer and clientSecret interpolation; omaAmbientEnv is the only ambient-env view vendored code consults on spliced sites (OMA supplies an empty map, so user-land env knobs like MCP_DIRECT_TOOLS, MCP_OAUTH_DIR, NPM_CONFIG_CACHE, BROWSER, MCP_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT, SYSTEMONE_ENDPOINT/*_API_KEY and the PI_MCP_ADAPTER_* test/recovery selectors cannot reach in); omaAgentDir/omaTmpdir re-root every getAgentPath-derived write and the output-guard spill root into OMA-owned directories; omaChildEnv runs the shared child-env allowlist over inherited process.env for stdio children; omaPinnedFetch is the egress leaf every HTTP path funnels into — loopback stays direct, everything else rides the vendored undici through a ProxyAgent built on the OMA pin, with upstream's own Request-translation (mirroring http-ca.js) so dispatcher and fetch share the vendored undici implementation; omaCaFetch substitutes that leaf for the whole fetch chain when upstream's CA-only leaf is absent; omaAuthStoreKind/omaOAuthFileKey pin the credential store to what the OMA policy declares; omaSecureKeyringClosed returns the same 'OS secure credential storage is unavailable' shape upstream produces on a host without keyring, so no vendored path can reach the OS keyring, the @napi-rs/keyring native binding or the keyctl recovery spawn; omaUiSessionsRefused is the same closed-by-default predicate for the interactive-UI permit the ui-session/glimpse gates consult; omaPolicyActive lets a spliced site distinguish 'no OMA policy' from 'policy installed'.

utils.d.ts.reason: Declarations for the utils.js OMA policy seam (see the .js divergence) so the adapter's install call and the sibling seam imports type-check under NodeNext/bundler resolution.

agent-dir.js.reason: OMA-owned state root. getAgentDir is upstream's root for the agent directory — the OAuth legacy dir, the encrypted-file store root, the metadata cache, the onboarding state, the adapter/pi config fallback paths and the npx resolver's package cache all derive from it. Under an installed OMA policy it returns the policy's agentDir, so none of those can be steered by PI_PACKAGE_DIR, *_CODING_AGENT_DIR or HOME, and no host-side Pi credential directory is ever read or imported. Without a policy the upstream resolution stands.

server-manager.js.reason: Stdio child env scrub and HTTP egress pin. resolveEnv inherits process.env verbatim upstream — under OMA it inherits only omaChildEnv's allowlisted subset (the child's env entries still override per upstream order). createCaFetch's leaf gains the pinned fetch when upstream left none (OMA rejects caFile at config validation, so the upstream CA branch is unreachable under OMA anyway); the bearer-command and provider-token wrappers' implicit globalThis.fetch defaults and the SSE path's `requestFetch ?? globalThis.fetch` fall to omaPinnedFetch so no composition step can leak past the pin.

mcp-auth-fetch.js.reason: OAuth/auth HTTP through the pinned leaf: the OAuth fetch wrapper's absent-delegate fallback becomes omaPinnedFetch, so authorization- server metadata, token and revocation requests ride the same egress policy as the MCP stream they protect.

mcp-probe.js.reason: Endpoint probes through the pinned leaf: the transport-kind probe's bare fetch becomes omaPinnedFetch so detection requests for a remote MCP server are egress-gated like the connection that would follow.

jev-client.js.reason: Semantic-search (Jev) request egress and ambient env. The pinned- endpoint fetch keeps its upstream shape — same endpoint pinning, redirect refusal — but the leaf becomes omaPinnedFetch so the request is egress-gated. Credential resolution reads omaAmbientEnv, so SYSTEMONE_API_KEY/TYPESAFE_API_KEY/OPENROUTER_API_KEY exported in the operator's shell are invisible; with the secure keyring also closed under OMA, resolution reaches upstream's own credential_missing/credential_unavailable results.

jev-key-store.js.reason: The Jev endpoint/credential env defaults read omaAmbientEnv instead of process.env: an operator-exported SYSTEMONE_ENDPOINT cannot retarget semantic search to an arbitrary provider under OMA.

secure-keyring.js.reason: OS keyring closure. Under an installed OMA policy without the os-keyring permit, createSecureKeyringStore returns a store whose read/write/remove throw the same 'OS secure credential storage is unavailable' message upstream's own native-missing path produces — so @napi-rs/keyring, the Linux keyctl recovery spawn and the helper script are all unreachable, for the Jev service-key store and the bearer-token store alike.

mcp-auth.js.reason: Credential-store pinning and ambient env. Under an installed OMA policy getAuthSecretStore resolves the policy's authStore — 'memory' or 'encrypted-file' — before the OS keyring and before the PI_MCP_ADAPTER_TEST_AUTH_STORE selectors, so host keyring reads, legacy plaintext imports of a host's tokens and keyctl recovery are all unreachable. getEncryptedFileKey reads the policy-held key under OMA (never an operator-exported PI_MCP_ADAPTER_OAUTH_FILE_KEY); the upstream env fallback stands only with no policy installed. MCP_OAUTH_DIR reads through omaAmbientEnv, so the legacy auth dir override cannot be steered from the operator's shell — the base dir is the OMA-pinned settings.oauthDir or the OMA-pinned agent dir.

mcp-oauth-provider.js.reason: The OAuth callback port override reads omaAmbientEnv: under OMA the operator's MCP_OAUTH_CALLBACK_PORT cannot retarget the loopback listener; the upstream default port rules stand.

init.js.reason: Ambient-env neutralization on reachable paths. MCP_DIRECT_TOOLS is upstream's env escape hatch into direct-tool registration — under OMA it reads omaAmbientEnv so the operator's shell cannot re-arm a surface the OMA config forbade; BROWSER follows the same view so the browser-open flow (itself behind pi.exec, which the facade refuses) cannot be re-aimed by env either.

index.js.reason: Ambient-env neutralization: the factory-level MCP_DIRECT_TOOLS read drives direct/namespace tool overrides at registration time — under OMA it reads omaAmbientEnv, so no exported env var can resurrect a tool surface the OMA config forbade.

config.js.reason: PI_MCP_CONFIG_MODE reads omaAmbientEnv: upstream's 'exclusive' env mode decides whether config sources merge or override — under OMA no env may reach that authority decision.

glimpse-ui.js.reason: GLIMPSE_BINARY reads omaAmbientEnv: an operator-exported path to a binary must not select what a UI surface would exec under OMA. And the glimpse viewer itself is gated on the ui-session permit: getGlimpseBinaryPath (the `npm root -g` host probe) and openGlimpseWindow (the host-global/bundled-path glimpseui dynamic import) refuse under an installed OMA policy before either runs — backstops beneath the call-site refusal in proxy-modes.js and direct-tools.js; with no policy upstream's flow stands.

logger.js.reason: MCP_UI_DEBUG reads omaAmbientEnv: an operator-exported debug flag must not raise vendored log verbosity under OMA.

metadata-cache.js.reason: computeServerHash and isServerCacheValid default their env interpolation base to omaAmbientEnv: server definitions' ${VAR} fields hash against the OMA view, not the ambient environment.

ui-session.js.reason: SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_TTY and MCP_UI_VIEWER read omaAmbientEnv: remote session detection and viewer preference are upstream's UI heuristics — under OMA no ambient env may steer them. And maybeStartUiSession itself opens with the ui-session permit: under an installed OMA policy it throws before the UI-resource read, the `who` remote probe, orca or any viewer work can run — a backstop beneath the call-site refusals in proxy-modes.js and direct-tools.js.

ui-server.js.reason: Post-listen 'error' absorption on both UI listeners: the host server's startup once-listener is removed after a successful listen (the EADDRINUSE candidate retry re-arms it per attempt) and the sandbox proxy's once-listener is removed the same way, so an accept-class error (EMFILE/ENFILE) later meets zero 'error' listeners and escapes its emit as the hosting engine's death. Permanent listeners journal best-effort through the child logger and keep both sockets bound for the kernel to retry — the startup rejection and the candidate-retry contract are unchanged. The ui-session permit already refuses this module under an installed OMA policy; this is defense in depth for a bare upstream load.

proxy-modes.js.reason: A uiResourceUri tool call is refused under an installed OMA policy with a structured ui_session_refused result — before the UI machinery (the ui-resource read, the `who` remote-login probe, orca, `npm root -g`, a host-global glimpseui import, a browser open) and before the downstream tool call itself: a tool built to interact through its UI cannot run coherently with the UI refused. With no policy upstream's flow stands.

direct-tools.js.reason: The same ui-session refusal as proxy-modes.js on the direct-tool surface: a uiResourceUri tool call returns a structured ui_session_refused result before the UI machinery and before the downstream call, under an installed OMA policy. (OMA config validation also pins settings.directTools off, so this is a backstop for any path that reaches it.)

mcp-callback-server.js.reason: Bare-builtin specifier normalization: 'http' becomes 'node:http' (identical module, the spelling OMA's package audit recognizes). Post-listen 'error' absorption: upstream's startup once-listener is never removed after a successful listen, so the first post-listen error is swallowed by the already-settled reject and a second meets zero listeners and escapes its emit as the hosting engine's death — reachable through the allowed auth:"oauth" path (mcp-auth-flow.js → ensureCallbackServer). A permanent listener journals best-effort and keeps the OAuth loopback socket bound for the kernel to retry, and the startup once-listener is removed the moment the listen succeeds so there is no swallowed-then-uncovered transition — the startup rejection contract is unchanged.

agent-plugin-loader.js.reason: Plugin-path `~` expansion reads omaAmbientEnv().HOME: the plugin loader is unreachable under OMA's config validation, and if a path ever reached it the ambient HOME could not steer it.

claude-plugin-loader.js.reason: Plugin-path `~` expansion reads omaAmbientEnv().HOME — same unreachable-under-OMA defense as agent-plugin-loader.js.

npx-resolver.js.reason: NPM_CONFIG_CACHE reads through omaAmbientEnv: under OMA the operator's npm cache setting cannot steer npx resolution into a host-controlled cache directory (and OMA's config validator rejects command:'npx'/'npm' outright, so this path is belt on suspenders).

bearer-command-resolver.js.reason: The `!command` bearer-token sink is refused under OMA before the shell spawn runs — same permit as resolveCommandSecret's credential-command gate; upstream's error path (a failed command) is what a denied resolution surfaces as.

request-headers-command.js.reason: The per-request `!command` header sink is refused under OMA before the spawned header command runs — same credential-command permit — and the command's own env spread inherits the omaChildEnv-scrubbed ambient set instead of process.env verbatim, so even a path that reached it could not inherit the engine's environment. The PI_MCP_ADAPTER_TEST_FAIL_PS selector reads omaAmbientEnv.

mcp-auth-flow.js.reason: Browser-open gating for the OAuth flow: the `open` package call becomes conditional on the browser-open permit. Under OMA's default the call short-circuits to a rejection, which upstream's own catch already degrades to 'Failed to open browser; waiting for manual callback' — the manual-URL path keeps working.

elicitation-handler.js.reason: Browser-open gating for URL elicitation: the `open` package call becomes conditional on the browser-open permit under OMA.

mcp-output-guard.js.reason: Output-spill containment: oversized tool results upstream spills to os.tmpdir() land under the OMA policy's scratch root instead, so spill files are created where OMA's lifecycle cleanup owns them. Without a policy tmpdir() stands.

generated.upstreamTests: upstream-tests/ is the repository's test surface at the vendored commit (the npm tarball ships no tests): __tests__/ wholesale, the root *.test.ts/*.test.mjs files, test-runner.mjs, vitest.config.ts, the conformance/ driver and the tsconfigs the suite compiles under; kept for provenance and porting, not wired into npm test — upstream's suite needs vitest, the upstream repo layout and for most suites the network
